metadata.title: S&P 500, Nasdaq End Lower But Dow Rebounds As Traders Rotate Out Of AI — NVDA, SPCX, PANW  In Focus

content.text:
-
The S&P 500 fell about 0.3%, the Nasdaq 100 dropped 0.6%, and the Dow Jones index rose 0.3% on Wednesday.
-
Fed's Beige Book showed rising price pressures, but at a moderate pace.
-
The PCE index climbed 3.8% in October compared with a year earlier.
The S&P 500 and Nasdaq ended lower on Wednesday, and fresh PCE and the Federal Reserve's beige book hinted toward persistent price pressures, while the Dow Jones gained for the third straight session amid a shift out of AI.
The S&P 500 fell about 0.3%, the Nasdaq 100 dropped 0.6%, and the Dow Jones index rose 0.3% on Wednesday. The Russell 2000, which tracks small-cap stocks, ended 0.7% higher.
The SPDR S&P 500 ETF (SPY) fell about 0.3%, and the SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ETF (DIA) gained 0.3%. Meanwhile, the Nasdaq-100 tracking Invesco QQQ Trust (QQQ) dropped 0.7% on Wednesday.
Meanwhile, the VanEck Semiconductor ETF (SMH) and the iShares Semiconductor ETF fell between 0.5% and 1%, with Nvidia (NVDA), Micron Tech (MU) and Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) leading declines.
Helping the Dow were gains in industrials, materials and financials stocks that gained between 0.8% and 2% as more investors rotate out of the AI play.
Retail sentiment on Stocktwits was in 'neutral' territory around the SPDR S&P 500 ETF (SPY), 'extremely bullish' on the Invesco QQQ (QQQ) and 'bearish' on the SPDR Dow Jones ETF (DIA).
US Market Drivers
Eight out of 12 Federal Reserve's regional banks reported rising price pressures and warned about the risk of an overheating economy, driven in part by heavy capital spending on artificial intelligence infrastructure. Commerce Department figures released Wednesday reinforced those concerns, showing gross domestic product expanded at a 4.3% annualized rate in the third quarter—its fastest pace in three years—propelled by the strongest surge in business investment since 2020.
The regional feedback arrives alongside separate government data showing inflation remains stubbornly above the Fed's 2% target. The personal consumption expenditures price index, the central bank's preferred inflation gauge, climbed 3.8% in October compared with a year earlier. Core inflation, which strips out volatile food and energy costs, recorded its sharpest increase since 2023.
Meanwhile, the Nasdaq 100 briefly touched bear market territory on Wednesday as more investors moved out of AI into other sectors like industrials, materials and financial services.
